text:
incidents-bot: :warning: ALERT (p95/p99 latency spike) — service: control-plane-configfetch — observed 10m p95=420ms p99=1.9s, streaming tail errors increased. Paging on-call: @george-oncall.

george-oncall: seeing spikes since ~1839123000, customers reporting streaming stalls. Investigating.

ben-sre: same, alerting traces show a >500ms median on config reads from auth-db and a cluster of 429s from feature-flag service. tl;dr control-plane calls blocking inference runtime.

carol-runtime: we started seeing stalled streaming connections — generator process stuck waiting for config fetch (sync call) and kv cache miss. A lot of concurrent long polls.

dan-platform: any recent rollout to feature-flags / config service?

elaine-pm: small FF rollout at 1839100000 for experiment X, but dev said it's a lightweight key check.

frank-cs: customer @Acme reported streaming sessions pause for ~3-5s then resume with partial tokens. Affected ~10% of sessions.

harper-eng: reproducing locally — if configstore is slow and we call it synchronously on start-of-stream, we block the streaming path.

ben-sre: logs (snippet):
```
controlplane: fetch_config user=svc/runtime id=kj23	status=200	latency=650ms
controlplane: auth-db query timeout after 800ms
featureflags: 429 "rate limit" for svc/runtime
```

ben-sre: DB CPU and connections trending up; I see connection pool saturation on auth-db read replicas. Might be a busy index scan from the FF query pattern.

carol-runtime: mitigation idea: short-circuit config fetch with cached defaults (fall back on local cache) for streaming flows, and mark config fetch as async. Can we flip a temporary toggle?

dan-platform: we can enable config-cache-serve (an emergency toggle) to serve stale cached configs for 5m. It lives in staging -> prod feature-flags. But toggling requires a safe rollout.

george-oncall: do it. Priority: prevent streaming stalls. Rollback easy if it causes issues.

harper-eng: I'm preparing the patch to make fetch non-blocking for the streaming path — small change but needs deploy. ETA ~12m.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued by harper-eng to channel=eng-runtime, rollout=canary(10%), version=2026.03.14-ff-nonblock.

ben-sre: meanwhile, I'm going to increase DB read connections limit and add a temporary rate-limit exception for internal control-plane calls to reduce 429s. Will monitor.

dan-platform: enabling config-cache-serve emergency toggle now (button).

incidents-bot: ACTION (toggle): config-cache-serve enabled by dan-platform at 1839123258.

carol-runtime: seeing immediate improvement on streaming tail — stalls drop off. p95 down to ~180ms, p99 improving.

ben-sre: DB connections increased +20% at 1839123302. Feature-flag service shows queued requests dropping. 429s down to baseline.

harper-eng: canary rollout of non-blocking patch started at 1839123350. Monitoring logs for errors.

harper-eng: canary OK on 10% after 3m, no errors. Proceeding to 50%.

deploy-bot: rollout to 50% complete at 1839123510.

frank-cs: CS note — pinging affected customers with ETA and remediation steps. No escalations yet.

elaine-pm: tracking customer impact: 12 accounts impacted, risk low but SLO breaches possible if not mitigated. Good to collect exact p95/p99 delta for postmortem.

ben-sre: root cause hypothesis: FF/Config path has an inefficient query pattern under new FF key semantics; heavy concurrent lookups cause read replica CPU to spike and connections to pile up, leading to 429s and timeouts. Runtime was calling fetch synchronously at stream init, creating tail latency.

harper-eng: rolling out non-blocking fetch to 100% now.

deploy-bot: rollout to 100% complete at 1839123605.

carol-runtime: full rollout live. streaming p95=135ms p99=320ms for last 5m. Streaming stalls virtually gone.

ben-sre: reverting the aggressive FF query in the feature-flag service is next — patch queued. Also will add a targeted index to auth-db to avoid scan.

dan-platform: I'll schedule a patch deploy for FF service to change query to use batched lookup and caching at 1839124000.

george-oncall: handoff notes for next oncall (ben-sre):
- Incident started at 1839123000 with p95/p99 spike due to config fetch and FF service 429s.
- Immediate mitigations: enabled config-cache-serve toggle (1839123258), increased DB read conns (1839123302), rolled non-blocking runtime fetch (100% at 1839123605).
- Current state: mitigated, monitoring.
- Customer impact: ~12 accounts saw streaming stalls, duration ~8-20m each, some partial token loss. No data leakage.
- Follow ups: index addition on auth-db, FF query rewrite + cache, make config fetch async by default for streaming, add circuit-breaker and better backpressure to runtime when control-plane is slow.

ben-sre: thanks. I'll take ownership for the postmortem and action items. I'll also open a DB ticket and schedule a meeting with FF service owners.

elaine-pm: please include customer impact table and SLO delta (tokens/sec and streaming p99 before/after). I'll cc support.

frank-cs: I posted a templated customer message in #support-private/critical-updates. Will follow up once we have root cause and ETA for permanent fix.

harper-eng: quick note: adding a retry + jitter for config fetch shouldn't be long — I'll PR today for the non-streaming path.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT: mitigated -> monitoring at 1839123720.

george-oncall: handing off to ben-sre for ongoing remediation and postmortem. On-call shift ends in 45m.

ben-sre: ack, taking it. Will open postmortem doc and assign owners.

george-oncall: thanks team. Logging final summary to incident tracker and closing active paging.

frank-cs: closing customer-facing alerts once postmortem ready.

harper-eng: follow-ups: (1) make streaming path resilient to control-plane spikes (async + cache) (2) add observability for config fetch latencies per tenant (3) rate-limit circuit breaker tuned for control-plane dependency.

ben-sre: created postmortem draft: https://redwood.internal/pm/INC-2026-03-14-configfetch-latency (will populate details).

incidents-bot: page closed by george-oncall at 1839123790.

george-oncall: end-handoff. If anything flares, ping #oncall-urgent. :thumbsup:
